history.text: I'm writing a strategy memo on how on-device inference is going to reshape the mobile app ecosystem. I need to stay on top of what's coming out — new model releases, benchmark results, hardware announcements, anything from Apple or Qualcomm on NPU roadmaps.
Understood. How do you want me to handle volume? This space moves fast — there could be a lot of noise.

Don't just pass things along as they come in. I'd rather you hold items, group related ones together, and give me a short synthesis. Like if three different people are reacting to the same paper, I don't need three separate alerts — I need one summary of the paper and why people care.
Cluster first, then synthesize. I'll hold until I have something structured.

Exactly. And when you do surface something, I want to know: what's the finding, how does it compare to what we knew before, and does it change any assumption in my memo. If it doesn't meaningfully update anything, skip it.
Only surface what moves the needle. I'll frame everything against your memo's current assumptions.
Good. I'll be deep in writing for the next few hours. Don't interrupt unless something genuinely changes the picture.
I'll stay quiet until I have something worth your attention.
